title: Rural and Municipal Utility Cybersecurity Act

claims.claim: Renews (reauthorizes) a federal program.
claims.sourceSpan: To amend the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to reauthorize the Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity Grant and Technical Assistance Program

claims.claim: The program helps rural, municipal, and small electric utilities.
claims.sourceSpan: an investor-owned electric utility that sells less than 4,000,000 megawatt hours of electricity per year
claims.note: rural=(A), municipal=(B), small IOU=(E); span shown for the 'small' clause.

claims.claim: Helps them defend their systems against cyberattacks.
claims.sourceSpan: to protect against, detect, respond to, and recover from cybersecurity threats

claims.claim: Gives the Secretary $250M over five years.
claims.note: five years = FY2026 through 2030 (inclusive).

claims.claim: To hand out grants, technical assistance, and prizes.
claims.sourceSpan: to provide technical assistance and award funding, including grants, cooperative agreements, and prizes, to eligible entities

claims.claim: To utilities that often lack their own cybersecurity resources.
claims.sourceSpan: has limited cybersecurity resources
claims.note: 'often' is a soft gloss; source frames limited resources as a funding PRIORITY factor, not a program-wide descriptor.

claims.claim: Reauthorizes the Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity Grant and Technical Assistance Program.
claims.sourceSpan: To amend the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to reauthorize the Rural and Municipal Utility Advanced Cybersecurity Grant and Technical Assistance Program

claims.claim: Authorizes $250M for it through 2030.
claims.sourceSpan: for the period of fiscal years 2026 through 2030

claims.claim: The Secretary awards grants, cooperative agreements, and prizes to eligible utilities.
claims.sourceSpan: to provide technical assistance and award funding, including grants, cooperative agreements, and prizes, to eligible entities
claims.note: 'eligible utilities' loosely restates source's 'eligible entities'.

claims.claim: Deploys cybersecurity technology.
claims.sourceSpan: to deploy advanced cybersecurity technologies for electric utility systems

claims.claim: Expands threat information sharing.
claims.sourceSpan: to increase the participation of eligible entities in cybersecurity threat information sharing programs

claims.claim: Provides technical assistance to protect, detect, respond to, and recover from cyber threats.
claims.sourceSpan: to protect against, detect, respond to, and recover from cybersecurity threats

claims.claim: Covers rural co-ops.
claims.sourceSpan: a rural electric cooperative

claims.claim: Covers municipal utilities.
claims.sourceSpan: a municipally owned electric utility

claims.claim: Covers investor-owned utilities selling under 4,000,000 MWh/year.
claims.sourceSpan: an investor-owned electric utility that sells less than 4,000,000 megawatt hours of electricity per year

claims.claim: Includes not-for-profits partnered with at least 6 qualifying utilities.
claims.sourceSpan: a not-for-profit entity that is in a partnership with not fewer than 6 entities described in subparagraph (A), (B), or (C)
claims.note: 'at least 6' = source 'not fewer than 6'.

claims.claim: Priority for entities with limited cyber resources or bulk-power/defense-critical assets.
claims.sourceSpan: has limited cybersecurity resources
claims.note: three priority categories: (A) limited resources, (B) bulk-power assets, (C) defense-critical infrastructure.

claims.claim: Authorizes $250M for the program for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
claims.sourceSpan: for the period of fiscal years 2026 through 2030

claims.claim: Information shared under the program is exempt from FOIA and state open-records laws.
claims.sourceSpan: exempt from disclosure under section 552 of title 5, United States Code (commonly known as the Freedom of Information Act)

claims.claim: Awards may be made on a competitive or noncompetitive basis.
claims.sourceSpan: on a competitive or noncompetitive basis

claims.claim: Names the Act the 'Rural and Municipal Utility Cybersecurity Act'.
claims.sourceSpan: This Act may be cited as the ``Rural and Municipal Utility Cybersecurity Act''.

claims.claim: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.
claims.sourceSpan: SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE.

claims.claim: Amends Section 40124 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (42 U.S.C. 18723).
claims.sourceSpan: Section 40124 of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (42 U.S.C. 18723) is amended to read as follows:

claims.claim: Has the Secretary maintain the Program.
claims.sourceSpan: The Secretary shall maintain a program

claims.claim: Providing technical assistance and funding to eligible electric utilities.
claims.sourceSpan: to provide technical assistance and award funding, including grants, cooperative agreements, and prizes, to eligible entities
claims.note: source recipients are 'eligible entities' (broader — includes not-for-profit entities under (a)(5)(D)); 'eligible electric utilities' slightly narrows, but the full category list is given in items[1].

claims.claim: To protect against, detect, respond to, and recover from cybersecurity threats.
claims.sourceSpan: to protect against, detect, respond to, and recover from cybersecurity threats

claims.claim: Awards funding through grants, cooperative agreements, and prizes on a competitive or noncompetitive basis.
claims.sourceSpan: award funding, including grants, cooperative agreements, and prizes, to eligible entities on a competitive or noncompetitive basis

claims.claim: Develops award criteria.
claims.sourceSpan: shall develop criteria for providing such technical assistance and awarding such funding

claims.claim: Establishes a process to inform all eligible entities of opportunities.
claims.sourceSpan: shall establish a process to ensure, to the extent practicable, that all eligible entities are informed about opportunities
claims.note: source hedges 'to the extent practicable'; analysis drops the hedge (minor, non-material).

claims.claim: Objectives are to deploy advanced cybersecurity technologies for electric utility systems.
claims.sourceSpan: to deploy advanced cybersecurity technologies for electric utility systems

claims.claim: And to increase eligible entities' participation in cybersecurity threat information sharing programs.
claims.sourceSpan: to increase the participation of eligible entities in cybersecurity threat information sharing programs

claims.claim: Defines eligible entities to include rural electric cooperatives.
claims.sourceSpan: a rural electric cooperative

claims.claim: Includes municipally owned or other political-subdivision utilities.
claims.sourceSpan: an electric utility owned by any agency, authority, corporation, or instrumentality of 1 or more political subdivisions of a State

claims.claim: Includes not-for-profits partnered with at least 6 such utilities.
claims.sourceSpan: a not-for-profit entity that is in a partnership with not fewer than 6 entities described in subparagraph (A), (B), or (C)

claims.claim: Includes investor-owned utilities that sell less than 4,000,000 megawatt hours per year.
claims.sourceSpan: an investor-owned electric utility that sells less than 4,000,000 megawatt hours of electricity per year

claims.claim: The Secretary must give priority to an eligible entity that has limited cybersecurity resources.
claims.sourceSpan: has limited cybersecurity resources

claims.claim: Or owns assets critical to the reliability of the bulk-power system.
claims.sourceSpan: owns assets critical to the reliability of the bulk-power system

claims.claim: Or owns or operates defense critical electric infrastructure.
claims.sourceSpan: owns or operates defense critical electric infrastructure

claims.claim: 'Bulk-power system' takes its meaning from section 215(a) of the Federal Power Act.
claims.sourceSpan: `bulk-power system' has the meaning given the term in section 215(a) of the Federal Power Act

claims.claim: 'Defense critical electric infrastructure' takes its meaning from section 215A(a) of the Federal Power Act.
claims.sourceSpan: `defense critical electric infrastructure' has the meaning given the term in section 215A(a) of the Federal Power Act

claims.claim: Deems information shared by or with government under the program to be voluntarily shared.
claims.sourceSpan: shall be deemed voluntarily shared information

claims.claim: Exempts it from the Freedom of Information Act.
claims.sourceSpan: exempt from disclosure under section 552 of title 5, United States Code (commonly known as the Freedom of Information Act)

claims.claim: And from any state, Tribal, or local open-records, open-meetings, or sunshine law.
claims.sourceSpan: any provision of any State, Tribal, or local freedom of information law, open government law, open meetings law, open records law, sunshine law

claims.claim: Authorizes $250M to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out the section for FY2026 through 2030.
claims.sourceSpan: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $250,000,000

claims.claim: Awards and technical assistance are subject to the availability of appropriations.
claims.sourceSpan: subject to the availability of appropriations

claims.claim: Information shared under the program is deemed voluntarily shared and exempted from FOIA and from state, Tribal, and local transparency laws.
claims.sourceSpan: Information shared by or with the Federal Government or a State, Tribal, or local government under the Program shall be deemed voluntarily shared information

claims.claim: The section is structured as a grant/technical-assistance program (subsections (b)-(d)) but subsection (e) also creates a broad disclosure exemption reaching state, Tribal, and local transparency laws.
claims.sourceSpan: any provision of any State, Tribal, or local freedom of information law, open government law, open meetings law, open records law, sunshine law
claims.note: structural synthesis; subsection labels (b)-(e) verified in source.

claims.claim: Investor-owned electric utilities qualify as eligible entities if they sell less than 4,000,000 MWh/year.
claims.sourceSpan: an investor-owned electric utility that sells less than 4,000,000 megawatt hours of electricity per year
claims.note: sub-citation (a)(5)(E) is correct.

claims.claim: The program, titled for rural and municipal utilities, also extends eligibility to smaller investor-owned utilities.
claims.sourceSpan: an investor-owned electric utility that sells less than 4,000,000 megawatt hours of electricity per year

claims.claim: Authorizes $250M but does not specify how funds are allocated across FY2026-2030.
claims.sourceSpan: for the period of fiscal years 2026 through 2030
claims.note: source gives a single lump sum for the whole period; no per-year allocation present.

claims.claim: Prioritizes defense-critical infrastructure but sets no minimum funding share for that category.
claims.sourceSpan: owns or operates defense critical electric infrastructure
claims.note: no minimum-share language in source.

claims.claim: Exempts shared information from disclosure but does not address retention or when the exemption ends.
claims.sourceSpan: Information shared by or with the Federal Government or a State, Tribal, or local government under the Program shall be deemed voluntarily shared information
claims.note: no sunset/retention clause in source.

claims.claim: Directs the program at entities with limited cybersecurity resources but sets no numeric threshold for 'limited'.
claims.sourceSpan: has limited cybersecurity resources
claims.note: no numeric threshold in source; note 'limited resources' is a priority factor, not the program's sole target.

claims.claim: Authorizes $250M for the program for fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
claims.sourceSpan: for the period of fiscal years 2026 through 2030
claims.note: 'added' bucket implies a prior-law comparison; the prior §40124 text was not fetched, but the figure/period content is source-backed.

claims.claim: Now awaits Senate consideration.

claims.claim: OMISSION: 'cybersecurity threat' is defined by cross-reference to section 2200 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 — not reflected anywhere in the analysis.
claims.sourceSpan: `cybersecurity threat' has the meaning given the term in section 2200 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002

claims.sourceSpan: may enter into agreements that can facilitate the objectives described in subsection (c) with eligible entities
